html:
Tom Mboya was a Kenyan trade union leader and politician, one of the main negotiators of Kenya's independence and a likely successor to Jomo Kenyatta, until he was shot dead in Nairobi in 1969.

A Luo, he led the labour movement during the emergency, when other nationalists were jailed. From 1959 he organised airlifts that sent hundreds of East African students to American colleges, with help from the Kennedy family; among them was Barack Obama Sr.

As minister of economic planning he shaped the economy of independent Kenya. His murder in July 1969 set off riots among the Luo and deepened ethnic tensions in politics under Kenyatta and Moi.
